A2: Wide-field fluorescein angiography of the right eye demonstrates peripheral vascular leakage/staining and extensive peripheral capillary non-perfusion consistent with Eales disease. B1: Fundus image of the left eye shows vitreous hemorrhage and neovascularization at the optic disc, typical advanced Eales disease findings. B2: Wide-field fluorescein angiography of the left eye shows 360-degree peripheral retinal capillary non-perfusion and leakage from retinal neovascularization, supporting Eales disease.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Ultra-widefield fundus photograph of a confirmed Eales disease patient showing dot blot retinal hemorrhages. Classic Eales signs (peripheral sheathing, neovascularization) are stated to be beyond the observable field, and the BRAO/BRVO changes relate to the paradoxical embolism background; attribution to Eales disease rests on the confirmed diagnosis plus the visible hemorrhages, so confidence is moderate. B: Fluorescein angiogram from the same Eales disease patient showing vascular filling defects and an old BRVO. These changes are largely attributable to the coexisting paradoxical embolism rather than classic Eales vasculitis, so Eales attribution is included but with moderate-to-low confidence.

A: The panel is a wide-field angiography (ophthalmic modality) showing hypo-fluorescent vessels during the arterial phase, which is a clinical manifestation of severe retinal ischemia in Eales disease.
